notes:
Grounded on installed libs: query-string 6.1.0 (node_modules/query-string/index.js) and decode-uri-component 0.2.0 (node_modules/decode-uri-component/index.js). Feature delta (git diff 62dd55867..fc3f047f9) adds only sanitizeTrackingValue + sanitizeTrackingParams + two imports; rest of utils.js untouched. Second independent sanitizer reviewer; walked parsing internals adversarially.

ANGLE 1 (extract behavior): queryString.extract = indexOf('?'), -1 => '', else slice(queryStart+1). Walked: search='' => extract ''; ''.split('&')=[''], loop skips length-0 param, keysInOccurrenceOrder=[], parse('') empty => returns {}. search='?' => extract '' (slice(1) of '?'), same empty path; parse('?') strips leading ? then !input => {} . search='?a=b' => extract 'a=b', non-utm, {}. search='?utm_x=1' => extract 'utm_x=1' => keysInOccurrenceOrder=['utm_x'], parse.utm_x='1', utmData={utm_x:'1'}. search='a=b' (no '?') => extract returns '' so keysInOccurrenceOrder=[] BUT parse('a=b') still populates {a:'b'} (parse only strips a single leading [?#&], does not require '?'). Divergence: for a '?'-less search, utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref still capture (read from parsedParams directly) but utmData is always empty (occurrence loop empty). This is the SETTLED '?'-less-input LOW (unreachable: DOM Location.search is always '?'-prefixed when non-empty, '' otherwise) - not re-flagged per brief.

ANGLE 2 ('+' + decoder parity): rawKey = param.replace(/\+/g,' ').split('=')[0] is byte-identical to query-string parse's key extraction (index.js:148 `param.replace(/\+/g,' ').split('=')` then decode(key) at :154). Both apply the '+'=>space replace to the WHOLE param before split, both decode the pre-decode key with decode-uri-component. So decodedKey === the key stored in parsedParams, making the parsedParams[decodedKey] lookup at line 75/82 correct even for percent-encoded keys (e.g. utm%5Fmedium decodes to utm_medium in both, so it is captured; utm%3Dweird decodes to 'utm=weird' in both, non-utm in both). decodeUriComponent(0.2.0) does NOT throw on '%' or '%zz': outer fn try decodeURIComponent -> catch -> customDecodeURIComponent, which returns input unchanged when multiMatcher finds no %xx token (no throw). Inner decode() only runs on a match[0] that already matched multiMatcher, so its input.match(singleMatcher) is non-null (no TypeError). Confirmed sanitizer's decodeUriComponent(rawKey) never throws for real inputs.

ANGLE 3 (dedup vs value[0]): occurrence loop dedups via indexOf (first occurrence wins for key ORDER). query-string default arrayFormat 'none' builds repeated-param values via [].concat(accumulator[key], value) in occurrence order (index.js:80-87), so value[0] = first occurrence, and the final Object.keys().sort() only reorders keys, not the value arrays (Array.isArray guard at :159). sanitizeTrackingValue takes isArray?value[0]:value. Key-order-first-occurrence and value-first-occurrence are consistent. Verified utm_a=1&utm%5Fa=2 => keysInOccurrenceOrder=['utm_a'], parse.utm_a=['1','2'], utmData.utm_a='1'.

ANGLE 4 (utm_ filter): key.indexOf('utm_')===0 (true prefix, not includes), excludes utm_source/utm_campaign (they are captured directly and thus never duplicated into utmData), guard parsedParams[key]!==undefined. Reverse-checked 'key in occurrence but not parsedParams': only occurs in the '?'-less case (SETTLED); within a '?'-prefixed string extract and parse see identical content, and any key the loop pushes came from a real param so it exists in parsedParams (same decoder). Valueless '?utm_term' => parse null, guard null!==undefined passes, sanitizeTrackingValue(null) returns null => utmData.utm_term=null - spec 5.1 note 'present with no value parses to null and passes through as-is' explicitly sanctions this. Bracket key 'utm_source[]' (arrayFormat 'none' keeps bracket) rides into utmData - SETTLED M3, not flagged.

ANGLE 5 (utmData shape): utmData assigned only inside `if (utmDataKeys.length > 0)`, so it is undefined (never {}) when no extra utm_* present - matches SPEC 5.1 'utmData present only when at least one additional utm_* captured; otherwise absent' and section 4.5.

ANGLE 6 (rule 13 no fabricated fallback): sanitizeTrackingValue returns firstValue unchanged when not a string (null passes as null; empty '' passes as ''); never substitutes ||0/||''/||[]. utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref and utmData values are all guarded !==undefined before the call, so sanitizeTrackingValue is never invoked with undefined. Compliant.

SURROGATE handling (5.1 rule 2): slice(0,255) is code-unit based; charCodeAt(len-1) checked for high surrogate 0xD800-0xDBFF only. Correct: a truncation that splits a pair leaves a trailing high surrogate (dropped, 254 units); a preserved valid pair ends in a LOW surrogate (0xDC00-0xDFFF, not dropped); empty string => charCodeAt(-1)=NaN, NaN>=0xd800 false, returns '' (no crash); single '\uD800' => dropped to ''. Matches spec 'value must never end in an unpaired surrogate' and qa-run-2 l2-B1 fix.

Empty-param skip (param.length===0) only drops consecutive/leading/trailing '&' segments, which are not real keys (parse maps them to key '' anyway, non-utm). No reachable key loss.

Conclusion: sanitizer's raw-string occurrence loop achieves exact key/value parity with query-string 6.1.0's internal parse for all reachable location.search inputs; decoder cannot throw; no fabricated fallbacks; surrogate/truncation/dedup/omission semantics all match SPEC 5.1/4.5. No non-SETTLED defects found.
